subject: RE: Intermittent inference errors in NovaHealth production — request for review of availability impact
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novahealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent inference errors in NovaHealth production — request for review of availability impact

Hi Michael —

Over the past 48 hours we've observed repeated 500/timeout spikes from our integration hitting the redwood-hosted model endpoint (region: us-west-2). Impact window looks like short bursts (30s–5min) between 02:10–04:20 UTC and again around 11:40 UTC on 2027-03-14. Our internal probes (attached: novahealth_probe_log_excerpt.csv) show successful retries but elevated error rates that caused degraded throughput in our ingestion pipeline.

We understand maintenance was announced for a subset of paths, but NovaHealth traffic was not on the maintenance list. Additionally, external traceroutes attached show packet loss toward one of your peering providers during the window (traceroutes_20270314.txt).

Request: please confirm whether this is eligible for SLA evaluation/credit (partial-degradation vs maintenance exclusion), and share the service-side SLO calculations for the affected interval. We prefer a short timeline — we are preparing an internal incident review and our legal/ops teams may request formal documentation.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Platform Engineering — NovaHealth
Elena.Ruiz@novahealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: novahealth_probe_log_excerpt.csv (CSV, 24 KB); traceroutes_20270314.txt (TXT, 12 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent inference errors in NovaHealth production — request for review of availability impact

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the detailed logs and traceroutes — helpful. We're opening a formal incident record and will run our availability ledger against the timestamps you supplied. A few quick clarifications that will speed the evaluation:

- Can you confirm whether the probes in novahealth_probe_log_excerpt.csv are coming from three distributed locations or a single region?
- Do you have the request IDs/trace IDs from your integration for the sample window (any single request ID is fine) so we can correlate token-level traces?

Preliminarily: we have a scheduled maintenance that affected a small set of peering links on 2027-03-14 03:00–03:12 UTC (published to the account maintenance digest). That maintenance was marked as "partial path maintenance" and excluded from SLA for routes identified in the notice. If your traffic hit a different path, we will consider that as potential partial degradation rather than maintenance exclusion — which can change whether credit applies.

I've looped in Marissa (CS) and Monica (SRE) to pull server-side health snapshots and the availability ledger. We'll follow up within 24 hours with a correlation analysis and a recommendation.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai

Attachment: service_health_snapshot_20270314.png (PNG, 120 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent inference errors in NovaHealth production — request for review of availability impact

Mike / Monica —

I've pulled the availability ledger for NovaHealth (tenant ID NH-2027-04). Summary: 2027-03-14 UTC windows with elevated 5xxs line up with two things: the peering maintenance and a transient edge proxy CPU saturation on a small subset of nodes handling prefetching for the affected prefix. The maintenance notice lists peering provider "EdgeSpan" and describes scheduled route updates; the edge proxy saturation is our internal metric and did not trigger a rollback — it resolved due to load shedding after ~3 minutes.

Questions for assessment:
- The contract defines availability as measuring successful 200/stream-start at the network edge, aggregated per-minute and then rolled up to daily availability. Partial degradation language references "reduced throughput or transient increased error rate not attributable to scheduled maintenance." We need clear customer evidence that their traffic did not traverse the announced EdgeSpan-maintained path. The traceroutes suggest packet loss to EdgeSpan for several hops, which complicates the attribution.

I'll draft an assessment doc and propose one of two paths:
1) If NovaHealth traffic traversed a non-maintenance path and edge proxy CPU caused user-visible errors, propose a partial-degradation credit (pro-rated)
2) If traffic was affected by the announced EdgeSpan maintenance for those source prefixes, maintenance exclusion applies and no SLA credit is granted; we can offer goodwill operational assistance.

Marking this high priority. Monica, can you pull the detailed per-prefix routing logs + the edge proxy CPU trace around 02:50–04:30 UTC?

-Marissa

Attachments: none

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent inference errors in NovaHealth production — request for review of availability impact

Elena / team —

Thanks for sharing the probe excerpts. Quick correlation notes (summary of attached traces):
- Per-prefix routing logs: NovaHealth egress IPs were announced over two upstreams; route-paths indicate a flap to EdgeSpan at 03:05–03:07 UTC and then a re-route to CloudNexus until ~03:10 UTC.
- Edge proxy CPU: spike on node gpw-edge-17 at 03:06–03:09 UTC; concurrent drop in active connections on that node (we did short-duration load-shedding to protect node stability). That lines up with 502/504 spikes in our ingest logs.
- Outside that short interval, we do not see sustained errors in the service.

Prelim determination: there was a brief overlap where an external peering flap coincided with a transient internal proxy saturation. Because both contributed, I'd recommend we treat this as a partial degradation with shared attribution rather than a pure maintenance exclusion. Proposed customer communication: acknowledge the peering flap, explain internal load-shedding, propose pro-rated credit covering 03:05–03:10 UTC window with calculation attached.

I'll attach the routing export and CPU trace in the formal analysis we send to Elena.

-Monica

Attachments: routing_export_20270314.log (LOG, 48 KB); cpu_trace_gpw-edge-17.csv (CSV, 16 KB)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novahealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent inference errors in NovaHealth production — request for review of availability impact

Thanks Michael/Marissa/Monica —

Appreciate the quick correlation and the frank explanation. The NovaHealth ops team confirms our probes come from three AWS regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1); our majority traffic to your endpoint is via us-west-2 and that was where we saw the highest error rate. We accept the shared-attribution approach.

Next steps from our side:
- Please send the pro-rated credit calculation and the final incident summary so we can close the loop with procurement/legal.
- If possible, include a brief suggested retry/backoff guidance for our SDK team to reduce user-visible impact in future short flaps.

If you can get the credit calculation by EOD PDT tomorrow we'll consider this resolved on our side.

Thanks again,
Elena

Attachment: service-impact-summary-nh.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)
